claims.text: An MLIP trained extensively on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations of the liquid state will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Active learning will ensure broad coverage of liquid configurations.
The MLIP will reduce free-energy integration-path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed material class is refractory equimolar high-entropy alloys, exemplified by Nb–Ta–Mo–W–Re, in solid and liquid states near melting.
The proposed intervention replaces the static EAM reference in thermodynamic-integration calculations with an MLIP trained on diverse ab initio liquid snapshots.
Active learning and uncertainty quantification can identify rare or extreme configurations for inclusion in the MLIP training set.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.95–1.00 times the melting temperature.
Liquid fluctuations and configurational diversity are most pronounced at approximately 0.95–1.00 Tm.
Moment-tensor descriptors or symmetry functions capture many-body interactions relevant to representing the liquid energy landscape.
Conventional EAM models omit complex many-body interactions that an MLIP can learn from a broad ab initio liquid training set.
Adding configurations with high prediction uncertainty increases the covered phase space.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will smooth the thermodynamic-integration path and reduce mismatch between reference and target free-energy profiles.
MLIP-driven free-energy differences will agree with fully ab initio results to within 0.1 eV/atom.
TOR-TILD's EAM-based approach has larger discrepancies because it insufficiently samples the liquid state's configurational diversity.
The intervention is expected to apply to refractory equimolar high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
Performance outside the specified composition and temperature range has not been established.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and completeness of the MLIP training set.
The hypothesis is falsified if MLIP-based thermodynamic integration differs from the ab initio benchmark by more than 0.1 eV/atom or improves path mismatch by less than 20% relative to EAM.
